purpose: Preregistered capacity hypotheses, matched controls, benchmark views, falsification rules, and cost ceilings for Imp research claims. Current status is intentionally excluded.

evidence_tiers.exact_replication: Original implementation, task distribution, metric, and protocol are available and reproduced.
evidence_tiers.reference_differential: Imp and an actual upstream implementation run under matched inputs, models, budgets, and scoring.
evidence_tiers.adapted_public_protocol: A public task preserves the claimed construct when paper artifacts are unavailable.
evidence_tiers.ecological_field_benchmark: A realistic workload tests whether the capacity survives operational use.
evidence_tiers.imp_native_extension: A BEAM-native capability extends the reference system and is evaluated on its own terms.

lanes.name: Matched declarative inference
lanes.capacity: Typed declarative programs preserve DSPy-level task quality across classification, reasoning, and multi-hop QA while exposing a production-grade BEAM runtime.

benchmark_views.name: GSM8K matched test
benchmark_views.construct: structured chain-of-thought mathematical reasoning
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned rows; identical model, temperature, demonstrations, prompt budget, scorer, and retry policy in Imp and DSPy.

benchmark_views.name: HotPotQA matched test
benchmark_views.construct: multi-hop question answering from supplied evidence
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned rows and context; answer EM/F1 plus grounding; identical model and call policy.

benchmark_views.name: Banking77 structured classification
benchmark_views.construct: typed classification under a larger label space
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned stratified split; exact label accuracy and parse failures under matched calls.

metrics: task score with paired bootstrap confidence interval

decision_rules.go: All required model-policy lanes complete and Imp is non-inferior by the predeclared paired quality margin with no material parse or reliability regression.
decision_rules.fail: A complete matched lane places Imp below the quality margin or shows a material structured-output/reliability regression that persists on rerun.
decision_rules.inconclusive: Provider drift, incomplete rows, unmatched prompts or budgets, or confidence intervals spanning both go and fail regions.

lanes.name: Instruction and demonstration optimizer lift
lanes.capacity: MIPROv2, SIMBA, and related optimizers discover programs that improve held-out quality rather than merely exercising search control flow.

benchmark_views.name: AIME instruction optimization
benchmark_views.construct: held-out improvement on difficult exact-answer reasoning
benchmark_views.protocol: Same train/dev/test rows, student and proposer models, trial budget, seeds, and metric for Imp and DSPy; baseline is evaluated before optimization.

benchmark_views.name: GSM8K and Banking77 optimizer lift
benchmark_views.construct: generalization across reasoning and classification
benchmark_views.protocol: At least three seeds with disjoint held-out rows; compare optimized-minus-baseline lift and total optimization cost.

metrics: tokens and dollars to best candidate

decision_rules.go: Mean held-out lift is at least 3 percentage points, paired 95% interval lower bound is above zero, at least two of three seeds improve, no family regresses by more than 2 points, and Imp is non-inferior to upstream under matched budgets.
decision_rules.fail: Dev lift exceeds 5 points while test lift is non-positive, random-label lift exceeds 5 points, or an optimizer costs over 2x for less than 1 point of additional test lift.
decision_rules.inconclusive: Fewer than the declared seeds finish, semantic proposal errors exceed threshold, task headroom is absent, or model/provider mismatch prevents a paired comparison.

lanes.name: GEPA reflective Pareto search
lanes.capacity: Language feedback and Pareto selection produce sample-efficient held-out gains across heterogeneous tasks, with resumable and semantically live search.

benchmark_views.name: GEPA six-family campaign
benchmark_views.construct: cross-task reflective optimization and Pareto search
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned paper-family manifests, exact scorers, matched model roles and budgets, and actual GEPA comparator artifacts.

benchmark_views.name: AIME semantic preflight
benchmark_views.construct: proposal validity, checkpoint recovery, and accepted-candidate progress
benchmark_views.protocol: One-seed bounded campaign must emit valid proposals and durable iteration outcomes before paper-scale spend.

decision_rules.go: The preflight is semantically live and the completed matched campaign reproduces the claimed sample-efficiency direction on the available exact or adapted task portfolio.
decision_rules.fail: Repeated valid campaigns show no held-out gain or materially worse sample efficiency than actual GEPA under matched controls.
decision_rules.inconclusive: An original artifact is unavailable and no construct-valid public substitute is complete, or comparator evidence cannot be matched.

lanes.name: Arbitrary artifact optimization
lanes.capacity: The same reflective search interface improves non-prompt textual artifacts with executable domain metrics and explicit acceptance rules.

benchmark_views.name: Paper artifact portfolio
benchmark_views.construct: optimization across unrelated text-parameter domains
benchmark_views.protocol: Run actual upstream and Imp adapters on the publicly released tasks with matched proposal/evaluation budgets.

benchmark_views.name: Imp code, agent-config, and scheduling portfolio
benchmark_views.construct: BEAM-native domain generality
benchmark_views.protocol: Executable tests and held-out workloads score correctness first, then domain quality; compare against authored and random-search baselines.

metrics: lift over authored and random baselines

decision_rules.go: Imp improves held-out results in at least two materially different domains without correctness regressions and is competitive with upstream under matched budgets.
decision_rules.fail: Lift appears only on training instances, artifacts violate executable constraints, or upstream materially outperforms Imp across the portfolio.
decision_rules.inconclusive: A domain metric is not independently executable or fewer than two heterogeneous domains complete.

lanes.name: Retrieval, tools, and agents
lanes.capacity: Imp programs retrieve the right evidence and execute typed tools through multi-step trajectories with quality and failure semantics comparable to DSPy.

benchmark_views.name: HotPotQA retrieval-grounded QA
benchmark_views.construct: multi-hop evidence retrieval rather than parametric answer recall
benchmark_views.protocol: Shared corpus and retriever outputs; record document identities; score answer and supporting-fact retrieval under matched model calls.

benchmark_views.name: BFCL tool-use subset
benchmark_views.construct: function selection, argument construction, and multi-step tool execution
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned public rows mapped to equivalent typed tools; score calls before execution and final answers after execution.

benchmark_views.name: Failure-injected agent workflow
benchmark_views.construct: bounded recovery from tool timeout, malformed arguments, and transient retrieval errors
benchmark_views.protocol: Identical deterministic fault schedule with trace-level terminal-state assertions.

metrics: steps, latency, tokens, cost, and terminal error rate

decision_rules.go: Both retrieval QA and tool-use rows complete on Imp and DSPy, with non-inferior task quality and no material trajectory-validity or recovery regression.
decision_rules.fail: Imp retrieves materially worse evidence, emits materially fewer valid calls, or cannot terminate correctly under the shared fault schedule.
decision_rules.inconclusive: Document identities, call arguments/results, or matched runtime settings are absent from either side.

lanes.name: Recursive long-context inference
lanes.capacity: A model can inspect and recursively transform context beyond its direct window, improving answer quality or cost-quality tradeoffs over direct prompting and matched DSPy RLM.

benchmark_views.name: RULER S-NIAH negative control
benchmark_views.construct: simple selective retrieval that should not require recursion
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned deterministic instances at several lengths; compare direct LM, depth zero, and depth one under matched total-token ceilings. A recursion loss is reported rather than averaged away.

benchmark_views.name: OOLONG aggregation and OOLONG-Pairs
benchmark_views.construct: distributed linear and quadratic aggregation over long contexts
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned public rows and official numeric score where available; pair-set F1 otherwise; direct, lexical retrieval, compaction, and RLM depths zero through three; bootstrap pairs by logical query.

benchmark_views.name: LongBench-v2 code repository QA
benchmark_views.construct: natural repository-scale navigation and synthesis
benchmark_views.protocol: All public Code Repository Understanding rows after a bounded admission slice; multiple-choice accuracy by context length and domain, with matched aggregate token and wall-time ceilings.

benchmark_views.name: Repository-scale synthesis
benchmark_views.construct: ecological navigation and aggregation over source text
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned repository snapshot and questions with independently checkable answer keys; record every recursive query and context slice.

metrics: quality per dollar and per token
confounders: answer leakage through filenames or metadata

decision_rules.go: Depth-one RLM beats direct prompting by at least 5 points on aggregation rows with paired interval lower bound above zero, is non-inferior to DSPy RLM under matched aggregate budgets, and traces prove recursive context use.
decision_rules.fail: RLM does not beat direct prompting in any aggregation regime, or is materially inferior to DSPy while consuming equal or greater aggregate budget; simple-retrieval losses remain scoped negative evidence.
decision_rules.inconclusive: Tasks fit comfortably in the direct window, traces do not prove context access, aggregate budgets are unmatched, or unavailable paper mappings/scorers prevent an exact-replication label.

lanes.name: Evaluation and inference-time refinement
lanes.capacity: Metrics, auto-evaluation, Best-of-N, and refinement select or repair outputs in ways that improve independently scored quality without hiding judge bias.

benchmark_views.name: Deterministic evaluation differential
benchmark_views.construct: metric normalization and evaluation semantics
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned cases execute in Imp and DSPy and compare normalized scores, failures, ordering, and aggregation.

benchmark_views.name: Constraint repair and Best-of-N
benchmark_views.construct: inference-time improvement under independently executable constraints
benchmark_views.protocol: Pinned natural tasks with hidden executable checks; compare first attempt, Best-of-N, and Refine under equal call budgets.

decision_rules.go: Refinement improves independently scored held-out quality at a useful cost and provider-free evaluation remains behaviorally conformant.
decision_rules.fail: Apparent judge gains do not transfer to independent checks or refinement regresses quality under matched budgets.
decision_rules.inconclusive: Only self-judged metrics are available or candidate budgets differ.

lanes.name: BEAM runtime performance and recovery
lanes.capacity: The BEAM-native substrate provides bounded concurrency, streaming, cancellation, recovery, and observable cost without sacrificing declarative-program correctness.

benchmark_views.name: Provider-free runtime overhead
benchmark_views.construct: framework orchestration cost without provider latency
benchmark_views.protocol: Matched local operations with warmup, repeated samples, medians and tails; compare Imp and DSPy while retaining language-runtime context.

benchmark_views.name: Live failure-recovery campaign
benchmark_views.construct: bounded recovery and correct terminal states under real I/O faults
benchmark_views.protocol: Inject provider, retrieval, and tool faults; require trace evidence for retries, cancellation, timeouts, idempotency, and released capacity.

benchmark_views.name: OTP concurrency soak
benchmark_views.construct: stable throughput and resource ownership under sustained fan-out
benchmark_views.protocol: Fixed workload at increasing concurrency; record queueing, mailbox growth, memory, scheduler utilization, tail latency, and leaked processes.

decision_rules.go: All correctness and recovery invariants hold, no resource leak appears in soak tests, and measured overhead remains within lane-specific bounds.
decision_rules.fail: Capacity leaks, unbounded queues, incorrect terminal states, or reproducible tail-latency/throughput regressions violate the declared bounds.
decision_rules.inconclusive: Host contention or provider variance dominates, runtime versions are unmatched, or the workload does not reach steady state.
